-- ============================================================================
-- solution.sql — schema, bulk load (~100k orders), and index for target_query.sql
--
-- Run top to bottom on a fresh (or previously loaded) database:
--     psql -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -f solution.sql
--
-- Bulk-load plan
--   1. Create tables (DDL identical to schema.sql). No secondary indexes yet,
--      so the load does not pay per-row index maintenance.
--   2. Load dimensions: customers (10,000), products (500).
--   3. Generate the order lines once into a temp table (tmp_items), so that
--      orders.total_amount can be computed in the same pass without an UPDATE.
--   4. Insert orders (100,000) with their totals, then order_items (~300,000)
--      set-based. Parent rows go first to satisfy the foreign keys.
--   5. Build the query indexes AFTER the load: one sorted build is much cheaper
--      than maintaining the indexes row by row during inserts.
--   6. ANALYZE so the planner sees the real distribution.
--
-- Determinism: setseed() plus a single-worker session means the same data is
-- produced on every run.
--
-- Data distribution (per the task)
--   status       COMPLETED 50%, PENDING 20%, CANCELLED 15%, REFUNDED 15%
--   order_date   uniform over 2025-06-01 00:00 .. 2026-09-30 23:59:59 (UTC)
-- ============================================================================

\set ON_ERROR_STOP on

-- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 1. DDL (same as schema.sql)
-- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS order_items CASCADE;
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS orders CASCADE;
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS products CASCADE;
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS customers CASCADE;
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS tmp_items;

CREATE TABLE customers (
    customer_id   bigint PRIMARY KEY,
    customer_name varchar(120) NOT NULL,
    email         varchar(200) NOT NULL,
    country       varchar(2)   NOT NULL,
    created_at    timestamptz  NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE TABLE products (
    product_id   bigint PRIMARY KEY,
    product_name varchar(160) NOT NULL,
    category     varchar(60)  NOT NULL,
    unit_price   numeric(10,2) NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE orders (
    order_id     bigint PRIMARY KEY,
    customer_id  bigint NOT NULL REFERENCES customers(customer_id),
    order_date   timestamptz NOT NULL,
    status       varchar(20) NOT NULL,
    total_amount numeric(12,2) NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE order_items (
    order_item_id bigint PRIMARY KEY,
    order_id      bigint NOT NULL REFERENCES orders(order_id),
    product_id    bigint NOT NULL REFERENCES products(product_id),
    quantity      integer NOT NULL,
    unit_price    numeric(10,2) NOT NULL
);

-- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 2. Bulk load
-- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
SET max_parallel_workers_per_gather = 0;
SELECT setseed(0.42);

-- Customers: 10,000 rows
INSERT INTO customers (customer_id, customer_name, email, country, created_at)
SELECT g,
       'Customer ' || g,
       'customer' || g || '@example.com',
       (ARRAY['US','GB','DE','FR','JP','BR','IN','CA','AU','NL'])[1 + floor(random()*10)::int],
       TIMESTAMPTZ '2024-01-01 00:00:00+00' + random() * (TIMESTAMPTZ '2025-06-01 00:00:00+00' - TIMESTAMPTZ '2024-01-01 00:00:00+00')
FROM generate_series(1, 10000) AS g;

-- Products: 500 rows
INSERT INTO products (product_id, product_name, category, unit_price)
SELECT g,
       'Product ' || g,
       (ARRAY['Electronics','Books','Home','Garden','Toys','Apparel','Sports','Grocery'])[1 + floor(random()*8)::int],
       round((1 + random()*999)::numeric, 2)
FROM generate_series(1, 500) AS g;

-- Order lines (1..5 per order, avg 3), with the line amounts pre-computed.
-- Kept in a temp table so the order totals are known before orders is inserted.
CREATE TEMP TABLE tmp_items ON COMMIT PRESERVE ROWS AS
WITH o AS (
    SELECT g AS order_id,
           1 + floor(random()*10000)::bigint AS customer_id,
           TIMESTAMPTZ '2025-06-01 00:00:00+00'
             + random() * (TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-10-01 00:00:00+00' - TIMESTAMPTZ '2025-06-01 00:00:00+00') AS order_date,
           CASE WHEN r < 0.50 THEN 'COMPLETED'
                WHEN r < 0.70 THEN 'PENDING'
                WHEN r < 0.85 THEN 'CANCELLED'
                ELSE 'REFUNDED' END AS status,
           1 + floor(random()*5)::int AS n_items
    FROM generate_series(1, 100000) AS g,
         LATERAL (SELECT random() AS r) AS rnd
),
li AS (
    SELECT o.order_id, o.customer_id, o.order_date, o.status,
           s AS line_no,
           1 + floor(random()*500)::bigint AS product_id,
           1 + floor(random()*5)::int      AS quantity
    FROM o
    CROSS JOIN LATERAL generate_series(1, o.n_items) AS s
)
SELECT row_number() OVER (ORDER BY li.order_id, li.line_no) AS order_item_id,
       li.order_id, li.customer_id, li.order_date, li.status,
       li.product_id, li.quantity, p.unit_price,
       li.quantity * p.unit_price AS line_amount
FROM li
JOIN products p ON p.product_id = li.product_id;

-- Orders: 100,000 rows, total_amount = sum of its lines
INSERT INTO orders (order_id, customer_id, order_date, status, total_amount)
SELECT order_id,
       MIN(customer_id),
       MIN(order_date),
       MIN(status),
       SUM(line_amount)
FROM tmp_items
GROUP BY order_id;

-- Orders with no lines would be missing above; there are none, since n_items >= 1.

-- Order items: ~300,000 rows
INSERT INTO order_items (order_item_id, order_id, product_id, quantity, unit_price)
SELECT order_item_id, order_id, product_id, quantity, unit_price
FROM tmp_items;

DROP TABLE tmp_items;

-- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 3. Indexes (created after the bulk load)
-- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Placeholder: finalised after measuring the plan (see below).

-- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 4. Statistics
-- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
ANALYZE customers;
ANALYZE products;
ANALYZE orders;
ANALYZE order_items;

-- ============================================================================
-- solution.sql — schema, bulk load (~100k orders), and index for target_query.sql
--
-- Run top to bottom on a fresh (or previously loaded) database:
--     psql -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -f solution.sql
--
-- Bulk-load plan
--   1. Create tables (DDL identical to schema.sql). No secondary indexes yet,
--      so the load does not pay per-row index maintenance.
--   2. Load dimensions: customers (10,000), products (500).
--   3. Generate the order lines once into a temp table (tmp_items), so that
--      orders.total_amount can be computed in the same pass without an UPDATE.
--   4. Insert orders (100,000) with their totals, then order_items (~300,000)
--      set-based. Parent rows go first to satisfy the foreign keys.
--   5. Build the query indexes AFTER the load: one sorted build is much cheaper
--      than maintaining the indexes row by row during inserts.
--   6. ANALYZE so the planner sees the real distribution.
--
-- Determinism: setseed() plus a single-worker session means the same data is
-- produced on every run.
--
-- Data distribution (per the task)
--   status       COMPLETED 50%, PENDING 20%, CANCELLED 15%, REFUNDED 15%
--   order_date   uniform over 2025-06-01 00:00 .. 2026-09-30 23:59:59 (UTC)
-- ============================================================================

\set ON_ERROR_STOP on

-- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 1. DDL (same as schema.sql)
-- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS order_items CASCADE;
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS orders CASCADE;
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS products CASCADE;
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS customers CASCADE;
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS tmp_items;

CREATE TABLE customers (
    customer_id   bigint PRIMARY KEY,
    customer_name varchar(120) NOT NULL,
    email         varchar(200) NOT NULL,
    country       varchar(2)   NOT NULL,
    created_at    timestamptz  NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE TABLE products (
    product_id   bigint PRIMARY KEY,
    product_name varchar(160) NOT NULL,
    category     varchar(60)  NOT NULL,
    unit_price   numeric(10,2) NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE orders (
    order_id     bigint PRIMARY KEY,
    customer_id  bigint NOT NULL REFERENCES customers(customer_id),
    order_date   timestamptz NOT NULL,
    status       varchar(20) NOT NULL,
    total_amount numeric(12,2) NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE order_items (
    order_item_id bigint PRIMARY KEY,
    order_id      bigint NOT NULL REFERENCES orders(order_id),
    product_id    bigint NOT NULL REFERENCES products(product_id),
    quantity      integer NOT NULL,
    unit_price    numeric(10,2) NOT NULL
);

-- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 2. Bulk load
-- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
SET max_parallel_workers_per_gather = 0;
SELECT setseed(0.42);

-- Customers: 10,000 rows
INSERT INTO customers (customer_id, customer_name, email, country, created_at)
SELECT g,
       'Customer ' || g,
       'customer' || g || '@example.com',
       (ARRAY['US','GB','DE','FR','JP','BR','IN','CA','AU','NL'])[1 + floor(random()*10)::int],
       TIMESTAMPTZ '2024-01-01 00:00:00+00' + random() * (TIMESTAMPTZ '2025-06-01 00:00:00+00' - TIMESTAMPTZ '2024-01-01 00:00:00+00')
FROM generate_series(1, 10000) AS g;

-- Products: 500 rows
INSERT INTO products (product_id, product_name, category, unit_price)
SELECT g,
       'Product ' || g,
       (ARRAY['Electronics','Books','Home','Garden','Toys','Apparel','Sports','Grocery'])[1 + floor(random()*8)::int],
       round((1 + random()*999)::numeric, 2)
FROM generate_series(1, 500) AS g;

-- Order lines (1..5 per order, avg 3), with the line amounts pre-computed.
-- Kept in a temp table so the order totals are known before orders is inserted.
CREATE TEMP TABLE tmp_items ON COMMIT PRESERVE ROWS AS
